name: Spectral Flicker
description: Analyzes per-channel temporal frequency spectra to detect irregular chrominance flicker absent from naturally lit scenes, a byproduct of inconsistent color generation across synthesized frames.
mechanism:
This method detects spectral flicker artifacts for video deepfake detection:

1. **Frequency-Domain Temporal Analysis**: The spatial frequency spectrum is computed per frame, and frame-to-frame spectral changes are quantified. Spectral flicker is defined as temporal oscillation in the energy of specific spatial frequency bands that doesn't correspond to scene content changes.

2. **Band-Specific Flicker Detection**: Different spatial frequency bands are monitored independently. The method detects oscillating energy in specific bands — GANs may produce characteristic flicker at their architecture-specific frequencies (related to upsampling layers), while diffusion models may show flicker in mid-frequency bands during denoising step transitions.

3. **Flicker Periodicity Analysis**: The temporal periodicity of detected spectral flicker is analyzed via autocorrelation. Periodic flicker (at regular intervals) indicates systematic generation artifacts. Natural spectral variation is aperiodic (random scene changes) or very low frequency (illumination changes).

4. **Flicker Spatial Localization**: Spectral flicker is analyzed per image region. The method maps flicker intensity across the frame — flicker concentrated in face regions but absent in background strongly indicates face generation artifacts. Whole-frame flicker may indicate post-processing artifacts.

5. **Flicker Frequency Scoring**: The detected flicker is scored based on: (a) temporal frequency of flicker (physiologically irrelevant frequencies indicate artifacts), (b) spatial frequency bands affected, (c) spatial localization to face region, (d) periodicity strength. High scores indicate AI generation.
parameters:
Analysis type: frequency
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through spectral flicker analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Zheng, Y. et al. (2021). Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection. ICCV.
Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
